Average people with great ideas cannot turn them into real designs. Vril removes that barrier by creating and iterating full 3D products and packaging from natural language, just like how Lovable democratized coding for everyday folks. Last month I had the chance to participate in Cal Hacks in San Francisco, where Haokai Xuan and I built Curio, a new type of social feed that uses a semantic graph to connect posts through shared meaning instead of hashtags or opaque engagement algorithms. Our goal was to keep the best part of social media which is access to vast amounts of related content while removing the addictive mechanics that usually come with them. They both had the same core feedbacks: - Start with a real problem you’ve experienced.
